source_snapshot.procedure_direct_xlsx: 【Before Test】 1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). 【During Test】 Hardware required: RDIMM with ECC / HDT Software tool: AMD RAS Error Injection Tool 1. BIOS settings: a. CPU Common Options → Platform First Error Handling: Enabled b. CPU Common Options → MCA error thresh enable: TRUE c. CPU Common Options → MCA error thresh count: FFE (Deviate from default setting FF5) d. CPU Common Options → SMU and PSP Debug Mode: Disabled e. FCH Common Options → FCH RAS Options → Reset After Sync-Flood: Enable 2. Unlock CPU via HDT. 3. Boot into Ubuntu 20.04/RHEL 9.0 / Windows 2022. 4. Download the AMD RAS Error Injection Tool, then install and open the software. 5. Enter the following commands: sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --listtwixwafllinks 6. Uncorrectable error injection at IOD sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --twixwafl --linknumber 0 --errorlocation 0 --errortype 1 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria_direct_xlsx: 1. For correctable errors, the tool provides a PASS status. 2. If the OS reports the error within a timeout period, the test passed. 3. If the OS does not report the error within a timeout period, the test failed. 4. Follow the AMD RAS Spec to check the dmesg and Error inject report.
source_snapshot.deepseek_direct_xlsx: PARTIAL | -- TXWAFL Uncorrectable Error at IOD: inject the TX WAFL TXWAFL Uncorrectable Error at IOD via the AMD RAS Error Injection Tool (after HDT/unlock + the BIOS RAS knobs from the procedure, e.g. Platform First Error Handling=Enabled + per-unit MCA/UMC settings). Agent stages/verifies with sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "dmesg -T 2>&1 | tail -160 | grep -iE 'wafl|txwafl|uncorrected|fabric'; echo __TX_WAFL_TXWAFL_Uncorrectable_Error_at_IOD; ipmitool sel elist 2>&1 | tail -40 2>&1" but the tool injection step itself is interactive/HW-level and needs the user to drive the exact inject command.

test_case.test_name: TXWAFL Uncorrectable Error at IOD — retained controlled review-layer procedure
test_case.purpose: Inject an uncorrectable TXWAFL fault at the intended IOD endpoint, verify the approved containment/reset and fresh IOD-specific RAS report, then prove the TX path, attached I/O and host have recovered.
required_package: Vendor proof errortype1 is IOD UCE and decision on contradictory correctable Criteria
FF5/FFE threshold encoding, TXWAFL relevance and raw restoration values
Expected containment/reset and fresh IOD-specific MCA/CPER/AER/BERT/SEL fields
Supported OS, timeout, attached-I/O traffic and link recovery thresholds
Abort, OOB recovery, injector cleanup and full BIOS/HDT restoration
test_case.test_command: Enumerate TXWAFL links and bind link0/errorlocation0 to a physical socket/IOD/TX endpoint; preserve raw state and logs; validate errortype1 and severity; run one injection under OOB capture; correlate fresh IOD MCA/CPER/AER/BERT and reset evidence; test link and representative attached-I/O traffic; restore BIOS/HDT/threshold state.
test_case.expected_result: 1. For correctable errors, the tool provides a PASS status. 2. If the OS reports the error within a timeout period, the test passed. 3. If the OS does not report the error within a timeout period, the test failed. 4. Follow the AMD RAS Spec to check the dmesg and Error inject report.

safety_gate: Dedicated SUT with independent OOB console and quiesced non-production I/O
Preserve raw baselines and do not infer link0 from ordinal position
Inject once only after severity, endpoint and recovery plan approval
Abort on wrong source/severity, unexpected reset, boot failure, persistent link/AER error, device loss or missing fresh record
No automatic retry/reset; restore all changed settings and verify attached devices
expected_evidence: Physical socket/IOD/TXWAFL and attached-device topology plus raw enumeration
Approved tool/spec and tuple/severity mapping with raw settings baseline
Exact injection transcript and OOB containment/reset/boot timeline
Fresh IOD-specific MCA/CPER/AER/BERT/SEL source and severity
Recovered link counters, attached-device enumeration and bounded I/O integrity
test_case.recovery: If runtime enumeration does not map numeric link 0 to the intended IOD, do not substitute another link without a reviewed topology update; preserve the original tuple as a recorded source discrepancy.
